x: Scoring 16 a side, the match resulted in a win for the Club by 253 points to 275. George Oliver, with an allowance of 4.15, was first in the handicap with Jack Baker (6.0) 2nd and Pat Sapcote (3.45) 3rd.

Dave McMullen was our next man showing good form early in the season, with evergreen East again among them and Pat Sapcote scoring in our first team over sevens, for the first time, thus showing he has speed as well as stamina.

Bert Clayton will get faster as the season goes on and Pat Sapcote will make 'em go for their place in the team. George Bentley is not quite fit yet and if Frank Tasker would only take the bit between his teeth and have a go he would find he can do the distance, and get there too.
Police A.A. race for "Wood Dunkley Trophy." Pat Sapcote was third. Tom Carter was first home with Alf Taylor second in the Vets.

Bert East showed that he still has plenty of speed after 25 years racing and was a good third. Going back a little further we saw some good walking by Alan Robins, P. Sapcote, Frank Tasker, Ted Evans and in particular D.

Bert Clayton continued to walk in grand style and at 8 miles was leading by the same 100 yards from Charlie Churcher and Pat Sapcote, with Bob McMullen, walking his first 20, some 40 yards further back, followed by Messrs.
Pat Sapcote was determinedly chasing three Woodford men and the odds seemed that he would catch them, in fact he assured us that it was in the bag, and he certainly did it.
Led by Pat Sapcote (3rd), the rest of the team comprised Ted Evans (9th), George Atkinson (13th) and Hugh McGreechan (16th), one of our newest members.

Jack Baker and Pat Sapcote also had leg trouble and they too retired. It was good to see Harry Shields coming along with a determined look on his face, subsequently finishing 44th, in his first long distance walk, over 20 miles.
The rest of the field walked well up to expectations, although Jack Bidgood was not quite himself and Pat Sapcote was suffering from lack of training.
Jack Bidgood and Pat Sapcote who send greetings to their many friends.
